name: Seinfeld
title: How much money does Seinfeld make? Reruns, streaming and who gets paid
description: How much money does Seinfeld make? Netflix's 2019 deal was reported at more than $500 million. A labeled estimate of rerun money, who gets each dollar, and every deal sourced.
tagline: Seinfeld stopped making episodes in 1998. About 60 million Americans still watched it in the first half of 2026, and Netflix's 2019 deal was reported at more than $500 million for five years. Acquired estimates the show cost about $250 million to make and has brought in about $5 billion in reruns, because the people who made it kept the back end.

blocks.label: est.
blocks.note: Total(t) = $5,000,000,000 + about $3.169 x seconds since Oct 18, 2026, 00:00 Central Time (05:00 UTC; daylight time, UTC−5). About $3.169 a second = $100,000,000 a year / 31,557,600 seconds. That year is the run rate of Netflix's 2019 deal, reported at more than $500 million over five years [[thr2019]][[lat2019]][[reuters]]. Model, not a live feed. The $5.0 billion anchor is Acquired's estimate of syndication, cable, streaming and DVD money to the owners through the episode date (around $5 billion to the cap table) [[ep]]. Their Wall Street Journal op-ed put the total since the 1998 finale at more than $4.5 billion [[wsj]][[folha]]. Actual receipts are not published. The 2026 renewal price was not disclosed and was reportedly lower [[deadline]], so this rate is not the current contract. Lifetime average since Sept 1995: about $5.09 a second, the same $5.0 billion over about 31.1 years.

blocks.title: Shares of the $100 million-a-year model
blocks.banner: Acquired's estimate. Widths are shares of each rerun dollar. The dollar labels apply those shares to Netflix's 2019 run rate, about $100 million a year. Not published receipts.
blocks.note: Out of each rerun dollar: 50 cents Castle Rock / Warner, 15 cents Sony, 15 cents Jerry, 15 cents Larry, 5 cents Shapiro / West. Per second at $3.169: about $1.58, $0.48, $0.48, $0.48 and $0.16. Cents are rounded. 15% of $3.169 is $0.475. The episode describes Larry's piece as a little less than Jerry's after Sony's cut; the drawing uses the rounded split. [[ep]]

blocks.title: Per episode, from the estimates
lines: Cost: about $250 million / 180 episodes = about $1.4 million to make each one ($250 million / 180 = $1.39 million). Acquired's estimate of the cost. [[ep]]
Rerun revenue: $5.0 billion / 180 episodes = about $27.8 million of lifetime revenue per episode. The $5.0 billion is Acquired's estimate. [[ep]] The 180 is the reported episode count. [[lat2019]]
blocks.note: Both quotients use an estimate in the numerator. They are not a studio budget or a royalty statement.

sections.title: Why the ownership paid off
sections.lede: NBC aired the show. NBC did not own the reruns.

blocks.text: From 1970, fin-syn rules kept the big networks from owning the syndication of shows they licensed from studios. NBC could broadcast Seinfeld. The reruns stayed with the studio. That is the account in the Acquired episode. [[ep]]

Castle Rock owned the show. In 1993 Turner bought Castle Rock. The LA Times reported about $100 million in cash and about $100 million of debt assumed. Sony owned 44% of Castle Rock and kept the syndication rights in perpetuity, so each renewal was a sale. [[lat93]]

It is reported that Jerry Seinfeld and Larry David each held 15% of the show. The terms were never published. Acquired uses that figure. The people who made the show kept a share of every later deal. [[ep]]

items.text: Owned the show. Turner bought it in 1993 for about $100 million in cash and about $100 million of debt, as the LA Times reported it.

sections.title: How much money does Seinfeld make?
sections.lede: Short answers to the usual searches. Estimates stay labeled.

items.q: How much money does Seinfeld make?
items.a: There is no published live total. Acquired estimates about $5 billion in syndication, cable, streaming and DVD money to the owners through Oct 18, 2026. [[ep]] Netflix's 2019 deal was reported at more than $500 million over five years, about $100 million a year. [[thr2019]][[lat2019]] The counter at the top starts from that $5 billion estimate and adds the 2019 run rate after Oct 18, 2026. It is a model, not a live feed. The 2026 renewal price was not disclosed and was reportedly lower. [[deadline]]

items.q: How much did Netflix pay for Seinfeld?
items.a: In 2019, more than $500 million for five years, worldwide, as reported by The Hollywood Reporter, the LA Times and Reuters. [[thr2019]][[lat2019]][[reuters]] In August 2026 Netflix renewed for five years, exclusive in the US and Canada. Deadline, Variety and The Hollywood Reporter reported the new price as lower. No dollar figure was published. [[deadline]][[variety26]][[thr2026]]

items.q: How much does Jerry Seinfeld make from the show?
items.a: For the final season, CNN reported Jerry at $1 million an episode and each co-star at $600,000. [[cnn]] NBC's reported offer for a tenth season was $5 million an episode, $110 million for 22 episodes. He said no. [[cnn]][[vulture]] His lifetime backend was never published. Acquired estimates about $750 million. [[ep]] A Wall Street Journal op-ed by the hosts said more than $600 million. [[wsj]][[folha]] Neither figure is a filing.

items.q: Who gets paid for Seinfeld reruns?
items.a: The contracts were never published. Acquired's estimate of each rerun dollar is about 50 cents to Castle Rock / Warner, 15 cents to Sony, 15 cents to Jerry Seinfeld, 15 cents to Larry David, and 5 cents to managers Shapiro and West. [[ep]] Sony's distribution right is the part the LA Times reported: perpetual syndication rights, plus a 44% stake in Castle Rock at the 1993 sale. [[lat93]]

The finale, on May 14, 1998, drew 76.3 million viewers and a 58 share. [[nyt]][[lat98]] A 30-second finale ad went for as much as $2 million, against $1.3 million for that year's Super Bowl. [[latad]] About 60 million Americans watched at least a minute in the first half of 2026, Nielsen via Sony. [[deadline]][[thewrap]]
